Re: Formal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Quinn Delgado
Member ID: W570305899
Reference Number: POC-A389519C6D-33639
Date of Notice: 2026-08-17
Requested Service/CPT: 28296 (Correction, hallux valgus/bunionectomy, with distal metatarsal osteotomy)
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-13

To the Complaint and Appeals Coordinator:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296 (bunion surgery, hallux valgus correction), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-17. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria." I request that this determination be reversed and the procedure approved.

Preliminary note on the criteria cited: The denial notice refers generally to "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria" but does not itself set out the specific criteria, and my own research was not able to locate a publicly available copy of the exact medical policy or clinical review document (title, policy number, or effective date) that was applied to this request. I am therefore not able to quote the plan's specific criteria back to you, and I have not attempted to do so anywhere in this letter — nothing below should be read as a quotation of Avera Health Plans' or any reviewer's policy language. As part of this appeal, I am formally requesting, pursuant to my right to the information relied upon in this determination, that Avera Health Plans provide me and my surgeon with a copy of the specific internal rule, guideline, protocol, or other clinical criterion (including, if applicable, any criteria applied by a delegated vendor such as Cohere Health) that was used to review this request, so that we may confirm this appeal addresses it directly. If additional argument is needed once that document is received, I reserve the right to supplement this appeal.

In the meantime, based on the general clinical elements that are typically used to evaluate medical necessity for hallux valgus surgery (symptom duration and severity, failed conservative treatment, radiographic deformity measurements, and functional/skin-integrity impact), I submit the following documented findings from my prior authorization packet for your review:

1. Chronicity and severity of symptoms: I have experienced 18 months of progressive foot pain that has not been relieved by rest, indicating a persistent and worsening condition rather than a transient one.

2. Failed conservative (non-surgical) treatment: I completed a structured 12-week course of conservative care from 2026-04-02 through 2026-06-25 (20 visits documented in the physical therapy discharge note), consisting of activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic. In addition, I used NSAIDs for 8 months without adequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-04 that provided only approximately 3 weeks of partial relief. Taken together, these records document a sustained, multi-modality conservative treatment trial that has failed to resolve my symptoms.

3. Objective radiographic deformity: Weight-bearing foot radiographs obtained 2026-06-07 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees, both of which reflect a significant structural deformity.

4. Functional impairment and skin risk: I am unable to tolerate closed shoes, and there is a documented risk of ulceration over the bony prominence, which raises a concern beyond cosmetic or mild symptomatic complaint. Physical examination further shows positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

5. Absence of contraindications: There is no active infection, no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker — none of which would raise a surgical safety concern.

6. Surgeon assessment: My treating orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has evaluated these findings and recommends surgical correction (CPT 28296).

I ask that Avera Health Plans reconsider the denial in light of this documented history of failed conservative treatment, objective deformity measurements, and functional impact, and that it specifically explain, with citation to the actual criteria document (title, policy number, and the specific criterion not met), any respect in which my clinical record is considered insufficient. If any single element of the criteria is the basis for continued denial, please identify it explicitly so it can be addressed with additional documentation if available.

I further request:
- A copy of the specific medical policy or clinical review criteria applied to this request, including the vendor (e.g., Avera Health Plans internal review vs. a delegated utilization management vendor) that performed the review;
- The clinical qualifications of the reviewer(s) involved in the original determination;
- A peer-to-peer review opportunity for Dr. Marchetti with a similarly specialized reviewer (orthopedic/foot and ankle), if this appeal does not result in reversal on the paper record; and
- Confirmation of the applicable appeal timeframe and, if this internal appeal is not resolved in my favor, information on my right to an independent external review under South Dakota and/or federal ACA appeal rules.

This appeal is being submitted within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-13). Please treat this as my written request for a full and fair review of the adverse benefit determination.

Enclosed/attached with this appeal are copies of:
- The Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-17;
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting the 12-week, 20-visit conservative treatment course (2026-04-02 to 2026-06-25);
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-04);
- Weight-bearing radiograph report dated 2026-06-07 (hallux valgus angle 38°, intermetatarsal angle 17°);
- Clinical exam notes documenting provocative testing and limited range of motion; and
- Dr. Marchetti's surgical recommendation/operative plan for CPT 28296.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address, phone, and email listed above, [and copy my surgeon's office, Dr. Marchetti, at [surgeon office fax/email], if permitted].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Quinn Delgado
Member ID: W570305899

[Enclosures as listed above]
